import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

The commit is declared, and the host makes it after this turn ends.

**Inputs**
- **Report:** there was exactly one registered `research.5i.final` report. I read it through its file ref because the `research:` label didn't resolve from inside the research checkout.
- **Diagrams:** the image agent's status was `ready`. Its manifest's `source` matches the lead's label.
- **No changes to existing files:** `__final.md`, the drafts and `.diagrams.md` are as they were.

**Layout**
- **Opening:** the title, then a three-sentence research query, then the infographic (`property_card_title_block_infographic.png`, confirmed beside the report), then `## Bottom line`.
- **Sections, in order:** the bottom line (the verdict and three corrections), what the five reports agree on, resolved disagreements, adjustments to the requirements, the recommended design, sequencing, decisions for Bryan, and how the consolidation was built. The last section holds the lead's scope paragraph, lead verification notes and source reports.
- **Renamed headings:**
  - The four resolution headings no longer start with a number. They read "Resolution 1 keeps or deletes H1 bytes per species" and so on, so the existing "(Resolution N)" mentions still match.
  - "(explicitly called out)" is now part of the Adjustments heading without parentheses, so the heading can be a link target.
  - "Verdict" became "Bottom line".
- **Added in-document links:** links point to Resolutions 1–3, the Adjustments section (A3, A9), lead verification notes, the recommended design, and "above". All targets were confirmed with `pandoc -t html`.

**Diagrams**
- **Placed:** `title-ownership` → `#figure-title-ownership`, after the "Rules" list in The recommended design. Its anchor is in the "One heading" list item.
- **Placed:** `title-slot` → `#figure-title-slot`, after the problem paragraph of Resolution 3. The reference sentence ends that paragraph.
- **Omitted:** none.
- **Checks:** each fence matches the manifest byte for byte and sits in its own `<div id="figure-…">` with its caption. There are 2 figure `div`s and 2 Mermaid fences (the lead's report had none), and both `(#figure-` links resolve.

**Checks against the lead's report**
- **Content:** all 12 table rows, the `text` skeleton code block and every claim are present. A 6-word sliding check found only gaps from renamed headings and added links.
- **Links:** the lead's report has no external URLs or repository-file links, so nothing was unverified or unrepairable.

The lead registered five other images (`identity-stack.png`, `property_card_title_and_species__cld_mock.png`, `same-chrome.png`, `title-homes.png`, `ship-order.png`). I didn't embed them: the lead's report doesn't reference them, and my only allowed additions were the image agent's diagrams.
